title: [Feature] Support multi-group KV layouts (hybrid sliding + full attention, e.g. Gemma-4)
body:
**Labels:** `new feature`, `kv-connector`, `architecture`

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
LMCache is currently unusable on any model that mixes attention types — Gemma-4 being the immediate example, with 50 sliding-window layers and 10 full-attention layers having different `(num_kv_heads, head_size)` shapes. The allocator correctly produces a multi-group buffer, but every storage backend and connector (`gds`, `local_disk`, `maru`, `storage_manager`, all three `kv_connectors`, `cachegen_encoder`) reaches for `MemoryObj.tensor`, which materializes a single-shape view and fails on the mismatched group.

Concretely, on `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block` with the V1 connector:

| Group | Layers | Shape `[chunks, 2, tokens, kv_heads, head_size]` | kv_heads × head_size |
|-------|--------|--------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| 0 (sliding) | 50 | `[5862, 2, 16, 16, 256]` | 16 × 256 = 4096 |
| 1 (full)    | 10 | `[5862, 2, 16,  4, 512]` |  4 × 512 = 2048 |

Sum matches the allocator's `115,343,360` exactly — allocation is fine; it's every reshape downstream that breaks. Net effect: LMCache can't cache Gemma-4 traffic at all.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Make `MemoryObj.tensor` group-aware and update the ~8 callers that currently assume a single shape:

1. Replace `MemoryObj.tensor` (single tensor) with either a list-returning API (`.views() -> List[Tensor]`) or keep `.tensor` but have it return a tuple/list when the underlying buffer is multi-group.
2. Update the single-shape callers:
   - `gds`, `local_disk`, `maru` storage backends
   - `storage_manager`
   - All three `kv_connectors` (read + write paths)
   - `cachegen_encoder`
3. Persist/serialize per-group metadata (shape, dtype, layer-group assignment) alongside the blob so offloaded KV can be rehydrated into the right group on load.

This lines up with the direction taken in SGLang (`HiSWARadixCache`, and confirms this is a broader ecosystem gap, not a Gemma-4 quirk.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- `--no-enable-prefix-caching` — doesn't help; LMCache intercepts earlier.
- `LMCACHE_USE_EXPERIMENTAL=False` — same reshape path.
- Forcing Gemma-4 to single attention type — wrong outputs; breaks model correctness.
- CPU-only cache tier — same reshape path.
- Patching `MemoryObj.tensor` + the 8 callers locally — roughly hours of work with uncertain blast radius, and every release would need rebasing.

We pivoted our Gemma-4 workload to SGLang (native multi-group KV) as the interim.

**Additional context**

Repro:

```bash
# vLLM: latest nightly
pip install -U vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly
# LMCache: latest pip release
pip install -U lmcache

export LMCACHE_CHUNK_SIZE=256
export LMCACHE_LOCAL_CPU=True
export LMCACHE_MAX_LOCAL_CPU_SIZE=25
export LMCACHE_USE_EXPERIMENTAL=True

vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block \
  --served-model-name gemma4-31b-fp8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --async-scheduling \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"audio":0}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_both"}'
```

Send any chat request → reshape error on first cache store/load.

Hardware: 8× H100 SXM (also reproduces on 1× GPU TP=1). Also reproduces with `google/gemma-4-31B-it` (unquantized).

Beyond Gemma-4, this will hit any future model with heterogeneous attention (hybrid sliding + full, Mamba/Jamba-style hybrids, etc.), so a general fix seems well-worth the scope.

title: [MP] AMD/HIP-specific deadlock at TP>=4: hipEventDestroy → SyncAllStreams collides with stream-ordered Python host callback on the GIL
body:
## Summary

LMCache MP mode deadlocks on AMD ROCm at TP >= 4 under sustained load. The same workload runs cleanly on NVIDIA H100. The deadlock is a GIL × HIP-driver-lock AB-BA between the Python thread destructing an interprocess `torch.cuda.Event` and the HIP driver thread that runs a stream-ordered Python host callback. LMCache/LMCache#3336 (merged target) avoids the deadlock at the LMCache level by routing the host callback through C++ with `gil_scoped_release`. This issue documents the AMD-specific observations so AMD can investigate whether the destructor cost in `hipEventDestroy` for interprocess events can be reduced or bounded.

## Environment

- LMCache `v0.4.4` unpatched (issue does not reproduce with LMCache/LMCache#3336 applied)
- vLLM `v0.19.0`
- torch `2.10.0+rocm7.0.2` on ROCm 7.0.2
- MI350X (`gfx950`), 8× per node
- Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501, `--load-format=dummy`, FP8 KV cache, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--async-scheduling`
- `LMCacheMPConnector` over loopback
- L1 host pool 5 GiB, `--chunk-size 256`

## Repro

1. Start LMCache MP server: `lmcache server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6555 --l1-size-gb 5.0 --chunk-size 256 --max-workers 4`
2. Start vLLM with `LMCacheMPConnector` over loopback and `--kv-cache-dtype=fp8 --enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling --tensor-parallel-size N`
3. Drive 2 QPS with a 5k-token prefix per request, `max_tokens=50`

We don't yet have a HIP-only standalone repro independent of LMCache; reproducing currently requires the vLLM + LMCache MP stack as configured above. Happy to work on stripping this down to a HIP-only test if it would help.

## TP-scaling matrix

| Hardware | TP | Result |
|---|---|---|
| MI350X | 2 | clean over 5 min (600 reqs) |
| MI350X | 4 | hangs ~110 s in (180 reqs dispatched at hang) |
| MI350X | 8 | hangs ~70 s in (120 reqs dispatched at hang) |
| H100 80GB | 4 | clean over 5 min (600 reqs, 0 errors) |
| H100 80GB | 8 | clean over 5 min (600 reqs, 0 errors), also clean at 8 QPS / 15 min (7200 reqs, ~73k store/retrieves) |

The hang reproduces only on AMD, only at TP >= 4. Higher TP shortens time-to-hang.

## Stack at hang

`rocgdb` attached to the wedged R-state thread on each MI350X hang. The same top-of-stack frames were observed on every hang (DeepSeek-V3 TP=8, Mistral TP=4, Mistral TP=8); transcript paraphrased below:

```
sched_yield → amd::Event::awaitCompletion → HostQueue::finish
            → hip::Device::SyncAllStreams
            → ihipHostUnregister
            → hip::IPCEvent::~IPCEvent → hipEventDestroy
            → THCPEvent_dealloc → Py_DECREF
```

The Python thread is dropping the last reference to a `torch.cuda.Event(interprocess=True)` while holding the GIL. The HIP destructor enters `hip::Device::SyncAllStreams`, which waits for the driver thread to drain a previously-scheduled `hipLaunchHostFunc` host callback. That callback is a Python function (`storage_manager.finish_write`) and the driver thread is parked acquiring the GIL — which the destructor still holds. AB-BA → deadlock.

## TP-dependence: destructor wall-time

Instrumented the IPC event lifecycle by wrapping `torch.cuda.Event(interprocess=True)` and `Event.from_ipc_handle` in `Server.store` / `Server.retrieve`, logging entry/exit wall-time of the Python destructor and a process-wide counter of live mapped IPC events at destructor entry. Three separate 2-QPS Mistral runs on MI350X, one per TP:

**Per-run summary** (`max_live` = maximum concurrent mapped IPC events observed; `mean dt_ms (steady)` excludes first-callback warmup):

| Run | Outcome | creates | destroys | max_live | mean dt_ms (steady) | p90 dt_ms | max dt_ms |
|----:|:--------|--------:|---------:|---------:|--------------------:|----------:|----------:|
| TP=2 | clean over 5 min (600 reqs) | 2004 | 2004 | 2 | 3.50 | 8.38 | 11.3 |
| TP=4 | hung at ~110 s (180 reqs) | 669 | 664 | 6 | 5.07 | 7.95 | 11.9 |
| TP=8 | hung at ~70 s (120 reqs) | 29 | 24 | 8 | 5.85 | 24.97 | 65.1 (first-callback warmup; steady-state max 25.0) |

`creates - destroys` at each hang = 5 — five IPC event destructors entered the runtime and never logged completion (consistent with the rocgdb stack showing them stuck in `SyncAllStreams`).

**Mean destructor `dt_ms` sliced by `live`-count at destructor entry** (three columns = three independent runs):

| live at dtor entry | TP=2 mean ms | TP=4 mean ms | TP=8 mean ms |
|-------------------:|-------------:|-------------:|-------------:|
| 1 | 2.01 | 2.03 | 2.32 |
| 2 | 5.28 | 2.25 | 2.31 |
| 3 | — | 5.80 | 2.26 |
| 4 | — | 5.46 | 2.60 |
| 5 | — | 5.62 | 7.97 |
| 6 | — | 7.28 | 12.85 |
| 7 | — | — | 4.10 |
| 8 | — | — | 15.28 |

TP=8 has small per-bin sample sizes (only ~30 s of activity before the hang), so individual rows are noisy, but the `live`-vs-`dt_ms` trend and the `live=8` peak (max 65.1 ms in that bin) are clear.

The scaling shape is consistent with `SyncAllStreams` doing per-mapped-IPC-handle work, though we have not confirmed that from HIP source.

## Direct observation of the deadlock

A second instrumentation pass on TP=4 unpatched added:
- Per-callback wrapping of the `launch_host_func` callsite for `finish_write`. Each scheduling and each completion logs a line and bumps a process-wide `pending_callbacks` counter.
- A daemon Python thread that wakes every 100 ms and logs `live`, `pending_callbacks`, and deltas — a heartbeat that requires the GIL.

The lmcache server hung after 110 s exactly like before. The last 1 s of the lmcache log:

```
21:19:23.611  host_cb schedule id=1096 kind=finish_write pending=1
21:19:23.612  ipc_event create id=1097 role=store_local live=5
[14.6 s of total silence in the lmcache server Python logs]
21:19:38.214  vLLM workers declare "LMCache server is unhealthy"
```

Three independent counters all stop at 21:19:23:

| Signal | Behavior at hang |
|---|---|
| 100 ms sampler heartbeat (requires the GIL) | Last beat at 21:19:23.552, then 14.6 s of silence |
| `pending_callbacks` (per `host_cb schedule` / `host_cb run`) | 365 scheduled, 364 ran — callback `id=1096` never runs |
| `live` (per `ipc_event create` / `ipc_event destroy`) | 733 created, 728 destroyed — 5 events whose destructors entered but never logged completion (consistent with the rocgdb stack) |

The sampler thread freezing 14.6 s before the vLLM health check fires is direct evidence the GIL is wedged: no Python thread in the lmcache server can run during that window.

## NVIDIA comparison (same instrumentation on H100)

We ran the same Mistral-Small-24B + `LMCacheMPConnector` workload on H100 80GB (driver 580.65.06, CUDA 12.9, torch 2.10.0+cu129) with the same `_TrackedIPCEvent` wrapper enabled at TP=4 and TP=8 (2 QPS, 5 min each). All runs completed cleanly (600 reqs, 0 errors, every destructor logged completion).

**Per-run summary on H100:**

| Run | Outcome | creates | destroys | max_live | mean dt_ms (steady) | p90 dt_ms | max dt_ms |
|----:|:--------|--------:|---------:|---------:|--------------------:|----------:|----------:|
| TP=4 | clean over 5 min (600 reqs) | 8800 | 8800 | 6 | 0.06 | 0.13 | 2.59 |
| TP=8 | clean over 5 min (600 reqs) | 17600 | 17600 | 8 | 0.08 | 0.18 | 5.91 |

**Mean destructor `dt_ms` sliced by `live`-count, H100 vs MI350X side-by-side** (each TP run is independent; only the AMD column at the relevant TP is shown):

| live at dtor entry | H100 TP=4 | H100 TP=8 | MI350X TP=4 | MI350X TP=8 |
|-------------------:|----------:|----------:|------------:|------------:|
| 1 | 0.04 | 0.05 | 2.03 | 2.32 |
| 2 | 0.05 | 0.08 | 2.25 | 2.31 |
| 3 | 0.09 | 0.10 | 5.80 | 2.26 |
| 4 | 0.06 | 0.10 | 5.46 | 2.60 |
| 5 | 0.05 | 0.09 | 5.62 | 7.97 |
| 6 | 0.02 | 0.08 | 7.28 | 12.85 |
| 7 | — | 0.08 | — | 4.10 |
| 8 | — | 0.01 | — | 15.28 |

The H100 destructor stays sub-millisecond across every `live`-count bin (mean 0.01–0.10 ms) with no monotonic growth, while AMD's mean grows from ~2 ms at `live=1` to 7.28 ms at `live=6` on TP=4 (steady-state max 25.0 ms in the TP=8 run). At well-populated bins the per-`live` ratio is 1–2 orders of magnitude, and at the highest `live` values it exceeds 100×. This is consistent with the AB-BA window being widened by the destructor's `live`-dependent wall-time on AMD; CUDA's destructor does not exhibit the same scaling, which is consistent with the absence of hangs there.

## Question for AMD

What does `hip::Device::SyncAllStreams` wait on inside `hipEventDestroy` for an interprocess event, and can that wait be scoped to the streams associated with the event being destroyed (or otherwise bounded)? On AMD the wall-time of this destructor grows with the count of concurrently-mapped IPC events in the process (see table above), which directly widens the GIL × driver-lock collision window. If `SyncAllStreams` can avoid iterating unrelated mappings, the deadlock window collapses and the AB-BA becomes much harder to hit on AMD.

LMCache/LMCache#3336 works around this at the application level by ensuring the driver thread never needs the GIL (host callback runs in C++ with `gil_scoped_release`, following the pattern previously established in LMCache/LMCache#2952 for `EventBus.publish_on_stream`). A HIP-side fix would protect every other consumer that combines interprocess events with stream-ordered Python host callbacks.

## References

- LMCache/LMCache#3336 — the LMCache-side fix
- LMCache/LMCache#2952 — predecessor PR that fixed the same AB-BA pattern at the `EventBus.publish_on_stream` callsite
